evidence_scope: North America plus SAB/MAB train/development structural diagnostic

figure_captions.fig01_evidence_counts.png: Figure 1. DIC evidence counts in unsealed train/development. The strict measured-fCO2 subset contracts from 5,356 DIC records to 119 records and only eight cruises.
figure_captions.fig02_strict_oracle_scatter.png: Figure 2. Exact TA plus measured-fCO2 inverse DIC against observed DIC for the strict subset. Scatter includes sampling and carbonate-parameter mismatch, not solver approximation.
figure_captions.fig03_strict_error_by_source.png: Figure 3. Strict inverse-DIC errors separated by CODAP-NA and GLODAP source. Source structure warns against treating the 119 records as an exchangeable product-validation sample.
figure_captions.fig04_propagation_rmse.png: Figure 4. DIC RMSE after injecting frozen upstream development residuals into exact PyCO2SYS. TA error dominates the joint propagation and prevents a publishable DIC product.
figure_captions.fig05_coverage90.png: Figure 5. Empirical coverage of propagated nominal 90% DIC intervals on paired-carbon anchors. This is a residual-injection calibration diagnostic, not independent pointwise validation.
figure_captions.fig06_interval_width.png: Figure 6. Median propagated 90% DIC interval width by error source and region. Joint intervals quantify the precision cost of uncertain TA, fCO2, and SSS inputs.
figure_captions.fig07_local_sensitivity.png: Figure 7. Exact PyCO2SYS local derivatives on paired observed TA-DIC states. One-unit TA errors transfer nearly one-for-one into DIC, while fCO2 sensitivity is smaller per unit.
figure_captions.fig08_carter_comparison.png: Figure 8. Strict measured-fCO2 DIC RMSE using observed TA versus Carter/ESPER TA where development records overlap. The small overlap makes this an audit rather than a product comparison.
